entries.title: Two run passports verify, and one-byte twins are refused
entries.user_value: A reader can run the published verifier offline against two fixed passports and see each original pass while its one-byte-modified twin is refused.
limitations: Reproducing a verdict does not reproduce either supervised run or expose the private system that produced it.
PASS establishes the bounded signed record against keys pinned in the project verifier; it does not establish semantic correctness, independent certification, or wider product availability.

entries.title: The public refusal corpus exercises 35 declared reasons
entries.user_value: A verifier implementer can replay the committed hostile inputs and compare exact refusal outcomes instead of trusting a prose count.
limitations: The 39 declared, 35 demonstrated, and 4 unreachable counts describe the verifier and corpus at this protected tag, not every refusal path in private components.
The corpus demonstrates deterministic outcomes for its inputs; it does not establish completeness or semantic correctness.

entries.title: A recorded filesystem boundary can be replayed on Linux
entries.user_value: A reader on a compatible Linux kernel can observe the recorded rule permit the named write and refuse creation, directory, symbolic-link, and unlink operations.
limitations: The probe applies the recorded rules to a new temporary directory; it does not re-execute the original run.
The observation covers filesystem-write classes on a compatible kernel, not resource or network bounds.

entries.title: Python and Go agree on 48 passport vectors
entries.user_value: An implementer can compare two project-built verifiers over the same language-neutral vectors, including exact verdict lines and exit codes.
limitations: Both implementations are maintained by this project, so agreement is not independent verification.
Agreement covers the 48 committed vectors and says nothing about inputs outside that set.

entries.title: v0.2.0 prerelease coordinate and release assets
entries.user_value: A reader has a protected source tag plus a public release manifest and checksum inventory for the bounded public distribution surface.
limitations: This is a prerelease of public documentation, verifier bytes, examples, and evidence records; it is not evidence of general availability or production qualification.
The checksum inventory is not a signature, and both verifier implementations remain project-built.

entries.title: Offline-verifier maintenance remains active
entries.user_value: Readers can separate the already published verifier from continuing work that has not yet earned another proved capability entry.
limitations: The active workstream label is a public repository status declaration, not proof of any unpublished feature, schedule, or outcome.
Only separately listed immutable artifacts support the verifier capabilities marked PROVED.

entries.title: Brand Identity v1.0 remains a review candidate
entries.user_value: A visitor can inspect the mechanically checked design study without mistaking it for the selected or current public identity.
limitations: The public record explicitly does not present this study as Owner-selected, adopted, deployed, or the current public identity.
Mechanical agreement with its manifest does not authorize downstream placement.

entries.title: The public landing relaunch was reversed
entries.user_value: The public history preserves an attempted presentation change and its later reversal instead of presenting uninterrupted progress.
limitations: The protected tag history shows the landing relaunch merge followed by its revert; it does not establish a cause beyond the public commit and pull-request record.
Repository history does not prove which bytes the canonical external domain serves now.

entries.title: Resource and network-egress bounds remain planned
entries.user_value: A user is warned that the published filesystem-write observation is narrower than whole-workload containment.
limitations: The status document records open objectives, not implemented controls, dates, or acceptance evidence.
No PROVED entry may be inferred from this plan.

entries.title: Proof Check is a proposal, not a shipped tool
entries.user_value: The proposed entry product would give a maintainer one bounded verdict over selected pull-request evidence, while preserving an explicit not-available state today.
limitations: No public Action, CLI, receipt, release, Marketplace listing, or reproducible Proof Check example is evidenced by this coordinate.
An Issue is a public proposal object whose body can change; this coordinate is never sufficient for promotion to PROVED.

entries.title: Canonical portal availability is not established by GitHub evidence
entries.user_value: A visitor is not asked to treat a successful repository Pages job as proof that the canonical domain serves a particular version now.
limitations: The public run reports a successful Pages build and deploy job, but it does not bind the canonical domain's response bytes or its current source.
External reachability alone is not treated as immutable GitHub proof in this journal.

entries.title: Cockpit and local-inference capability remain unknown
entries.user_value: Readers receive an explicit unknown rather than an inference from private development or product vocabulary.
limitations: The inspected protected public tree carries no qualifying immutable coordinate for a Cockpit or local-inference capability.
Absence from this public tree is not proof that work does not exist elsewhere; it keeps the public status UNKNOWN.

entries.title: Marketplace, partner, connector-effect, and production state remain unknown
entries.user_value: A visitor is not led to infer distribution, endorsement, external side effects, or operational adoption from repository activity.
limitations: The public release notes expressly do not establish an accepted integration, partner status, provider endorsement, or production deployment.
No qualifying public immutable artifact establishes a Marketplace listing or live connector effect, so the journal does not infer either.

entries.title: The tagged claim-count policy disagrees with the ledger
entries.user_value: A reader is warned that one hand-written policy count lags the machine ledger instead of receiving whichever count sounds stronger.
limitations: At the same protected tag, docs/publication-policy.md names two current public-reproducible claims while the machine ledger and evidence README carry five.
The mismatch does not by itself invalidate the underlying artifacts, decide which claim is correct, or repair the existing documents.
